title: Content Understanding & Document AI - Simply Explained
description:
Shared inboxes still fill with invoices, receipts and contracts that someone has to open and retype, and simple rules break as soon as layouts change. This episode explains for Power Platform makers and process owners how Content Understanding, Power Automate, Dataverse and Power Apps turn documents into trusted business data with human review where it matters.
In this episode
00:00 – Introduction: documents as business data00:34 – Why documents break automation03:04 – Content Understanding simply explained07:01 – The Power Platform connection10:32 – Trust, confidence and human review13:28 – Choosing a first use case16:11 – Where this changes your work
Key takeaways
OCR reads characters, but Content Understanding uses a schema to return the business fields a process actually needs, such as supplier, invoice number and total.Power Automate moves extracted data through the process, Dataverse tracks each record and its history, and Power Apps gives reviewers a place to fix exceptions.Confidence scores and validation rules decide when a document can move on and when a person must check it, and the first use case should be one document type with one clear decision and owner.
Worth quoting
“If the process is unclear before automation, it becomes unclear faster after automation, with more records moving through it.” – Mirko Peters (10:03)
“Even when the score looks strong, the rule should follow the consequence of an error, not just the score.” – Mirko Peters (11:17)
Explore more on M365.FM
Episode page: the full episode with chapters, quotes and FAQ on document AIPower Automate – the process engine that sends files to Content Understanding and routes the resultsPower Platform – the action layer that turns extracted fields into a working business processDataverse – holds each document's record, status, owner, field confidence and review historyHuman in the loop – reviewers fix uncertain fields in Power Apps when an error would be costlyAutomation – why rules-based automation breaks on varied layouts and speeds up unclear processesRelated episode: Power Platform Copilot Integration - Simply Explained
